messages:
olivia: Heads up — seeing repeated scale-down flapping in eu-west GPU nodepools since ~08:10UTC. CA starts drain -> drain hits probe/timeouts -> fails -> node comes back and CA tries again. Logs pasted: https://internal/logs/CA/2345678901

mike: yep noticed this from alerting, pod Terminating stuck on PostStart hook and CNI reconnects. Affected pools: gpu-a2, gpu-batch.

raj: quick blip in the dataplane earlier, looked like CNI churn (we upgraded cni-plugin last night). MTU mismatch + a kernel netdev patch caused intermittent 10-20s blackholes during iface reset.

sarah: see kube-proxy conntrack spikes too, some services transiently unreachable. Pods still show Ready->NotReady during drain which makes CA think node is needed.

infra-oncall: deploy-bot flagged CA scale-down failures: 
```
E0321 08:12:03 main.go:200] Failed to drain node gpu-a2-12: timeout waiting for pods to terminate (some stuck in Terminating, waiting for preStop/CNI cleanup)
E0321 08:12:04 main.go:201] ScaleDown unsuccessful: node gpu-a2-12 is still needed
```

mike: short-term we should slow CA down so it doesn't fight the noisy network. Long-term we fix CNI.

raj: Agreed. Suggested immediate CA flags to relax: 
```
--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m \
--scale-down-unready-time=15m \
--scale-down-delay-after-add=12m \
--max-empty-bulk-delete=1
```
Rationale: give pods/CNI more time to recover before marking node unneeded and avoid batch deleting multiple GPU nodes at once.

olivia: +1 on conservative settings. Concern: increasing unneeded-time costs more for idle GPUs. What's acceptable tradeoff?

sarah: For now prefer uptime/availability > minimal cost. We can set this as a short-lived mitigation while we revert CNI patch. Maybe 24h window then revert.

infra-oncall: also adding these CA knobs might not fix nodes that stay in Terminating due to finalizers or hostpath mounts. Recommended quick pre-checks: 
- run `kubectl get pod -A -o wide | grep Terminating`
- check `kubectl describe pod` for finalizers / terminating hooks
- check kubelet logs on node for eviction/drain errors

mike: Another tweak: enable `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false`? Currently CA skips nodes with local storage which prevents some drains. But setting false can allow CA to remove empty nodes with ephemeral disks. Risky if we have stateful pods.

raj: We should avoid changing skip-nodes flag without careful review. Alternative: add a temporary taint to new nodes to avoid rapid reuse while we stabilize: `kubectl taint nodes gpu-a2-* temp/drain-cooldown=true:NoSchedule` and remove later.

deploy-bot: Reminder: changing autoscaler flags requires new deployment rollout and full canary in staging. Use canary nodegroup first.

olivia: Plan proposal: 
1) roll a canary CA deployment in staging with relaxed flags (raj+infra-oncall)
2) revert the CNI plugin change in eu-west (raj) and monitor for 1h
3) if staging looks good, promote CA change to canary pool in prod (olivia+mike) with 30m watch.
4) if no regressions, keep flags for max 24h then revert to cost-optimal values.

mike: I'll prepare the CA helm patch and a short runbook for on-call to revert quickly.

raj: I'll open a rollback PR for the CNI and coordinate with networking to schedule revert immediately.

infra-oncall: I'll increase alert thresholds so we don't get noisy pages while we test (only P2 for now).

olivia: Ty. Action owners: raj (CNI rollback), mike (CA helm patch + runbook), infra-oncall (canary rollout + alert tuning). Check-ins in #incidents in 30m. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary deployment created for autoscaler (deploy-id: canary-2345). Watch: https://internal/deploys/canary-2345

sarah: after rollback we should run soak on a small gpu pool to validate probes and conntrack under drain. I'll script a load that triggers drains and measure success rate.

olivia: Good. We'll reconvene after 30m with results.
